findings.title: The decision-writing basic content names no branch for a non-zero exit of orbit decisions status
findings.recommendation: DECISION_WRITING_BASIC branches only on write: true and write: false. The command is built to exit zero on every config, so the gap is reached only when the installed CLI lacks the command: in this repository today the installed orbit 2.0.2 answers `error: unknown command 'decisions'` with exit 1, and only CLAUDE.md's workaround (node bin/orbit.js decisions status) covers it; an adopter's skills are generated by the same CLI, so they meet it only on a version mismatch. Either leave the body as it is and rely on CLAUDE.md here (the gap is unreachable for an adopter with matching versions), or add a short clause naming what a non-zero exit means (for example, read it as write: false and say so in one line), as the commit and chain end steps name theirs. Adding a clause changes all fourteen bodies, the basic-content fence and the ledger's LABELLED_FORM swap, so it belongs in this change only if Sal wants it.

recommendation_options.label: A
recommendation_options.body: Keep the basic content as is; the non-zero case is a version mismatch that CLAUDE.md covers in this repository.

recommendation_options.label: B
recommendation_options.body: Add one clause to DECISION_WRITING_BASIC and its fence naming what a non-zero exit means, and move the parity and ledger tests with it.

findings.reproduction: In this repository: `orbit --version` prints 2.0.2; `orbit decisions status --json` prints `error: unknown command 'decisions'` and exits 1. The basic content in every generated body (e.g. .claude/skills/orbit-review/SKILL.md, the epitome's fifth bullet) says what to do on write: true and write: false only.

findings.title: The reference's opening is worded differently in the spec and in the shipped constant
findings.recommendation: Decision-record reference ships beside the statement says the reference "opens with one sentence" and that an answer or fix at write: false "follows the record's own section and `Fixing a record`" (its scenario The reference lets an answer or a fix through at write: false says the same). The shipped opening (src/core/disciplines.ts:331, quoted by design Decision 4 and asserted by decision-writing-parity.test.ts) is two sentences and names "the Resolution and Fixing a record sections": for a fix of a ledger entry or stop it names Fixing a record only, not that record's own section. A reader still reaches the right section, since Fixing a record says to write a new record of the same kind, so nothing breaks; but the scenario is text-tagged and its THEN is not the text the test asserts. Align one to the other.

recommendation_options.label: A
recommendation_options.body: Reword the constant's last clause to "which follows that record's own section and Fixing a record", and move the parity test's assertion and the regenerated references with it.

recommendation_options.label: B
recommendation_options.body: Reword the spec requirement and its scenario to the shipped text (two sentences; the Resolution and Fixing a record sections).

findings.title: The stage charter's summary of the defaults is broader than what shipped
findings.recommendation: The charter says that at the defaults the AI writes no ledger entry, stop record or resolution, and that the reading step selects nothing; R-rop-17 says the reading step finds nothing to read. What shipped (D-rbs-8 and D-rbs-10 at the proposal walk) still writes a resolution answering a stop already in a trail and a replacement fixing a record already there, and still selects and reads existing records at the defaults (this change's own trail has records from explore and propose). The narrowing keeps more of today's behaviour, so it stays inside RG0 as amended, but the charter text and the shipped rule now differ. Name the difference in the stage's Shipped-as paragraph and the change's account at archive, so the charter is not read later as the behaviour.

commentary:
Probed: the full diff from c0d2562b to HEAD with the trail excluded, the new predicate against each resolver's source (all three resolvers are silent and absorb a missing or unparseable config, so --json stdout stays clean), the CLI in a bare project, an unparseable config, `signoff: weekly` and a subdirectory, the archive merge of both deltas rehearsed with dist buildUpdatedSpec (RENAMED plus MODIFIED land; the old title leaves both specs), a residue sweep for 'under every setting', 'in every mode' and the old requirement title over src, test, docs, orbit/specs, CLAUDE.md and skill_body_convention.md (every remaining hit is the account, the brief save, review emit notes, or a baseline block the delta replaces at archive), the scenario lists of the three MODIFIED requirements against the baseline (every scenario carried, two renamed and retagged), `orbit validate records-by-setting --strict`, `orbit validate --sources`, and the full suite (211 files, 4431 tests, green).

Pass 0 ran inline, not by invoking /orbit:verify: a dispatched worker runs no other orbit command. Pass 6 likewise ran as the targeted residue and cross-doc sweep above, not as /orbit:audit-drift. Passes 4 and 5 were skipped because orbit/lenses/ does not exist in this repository.

The mechanics are tight. The edit ledger reverses the swap before its own pairs, the parity test finds each fence by a longer prefix and shows that the shared label alone would match the wrong one, and the predicate iterates the sensor list. The three findings are all about wording at the edges: a result the body does not name, a spec paraphrase that drifted from its constant, and a charter sentence that predates the proposal walk's narrowing. One more, below finding level: `orbit decisions status` reads '.', as `orbit decisions brief` does, so run from a subdirectory it reports `not written` even where a setting is on. That fails quietly and toward writing nothing; it is the repository's usual from-root convention, not something this change introduced.

direction.reasoning: The change does what the stage asks. At the defaults the command says nothing is written and every body carries the one-line basic content. Each reading setting turns writing on, shown by test. The rule moved whole to the reference with only its opening clause replaced, held by the ledger and the parity test. Budget ceilings went down. The suite is green and the archive merge rehearses cleanly. None of what remains is a defect a user would meet: two wording alignments and a missing branch that only a mismatched CLI version reaches. The walk can settle them, or record them as accepted, before archive.
